verdict.rationale: GitCafe documents an official hosted MCP server at https://git.cafe/mcp. AI tools such as Claude and ChatGPT can use it to read repositories and, with the user's approval, work on issues and pull requests. The docs also cover unauthenticated read tools for public repositories, per-connection repository access scoping and WebMCP exposure in the browser, and a probe confirms the MCP connections documentation exists. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that agents connect and operate successfully through the server.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can connect an agent via an official MCP server

citations.quote: GitCafe runs an MCP server at `https://git.cafe/mcp`, so AI tools such as Claude and ChatGPT can read repositories and, with your approval, work on issues and pull requests.
Without connecting an account, its read tools work on public repositories: code, branches and tags, issues, pull requests, reviews and CI results.
Choose the repository access: **All repositories you can access** (the default...) or **Only select repositories…**
In a browser that supports WebMCP, GitCafe pages offer the MCP server's tools to the browser's agent.
